common_name: Blue Ice Agapanthus (Pale Blue RHS Award-Winning Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Blue Ice holds a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for its pale blue flower heads.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun, where clumps of strap-shaped foliage will bulk up over a few seasons. Blue Ice produces rounded umbels of soft pale blue flowers on upright scapes in mid- to late summer, a color that reads lighter and more washed-out than many deep-blue agapanthus cultivars. It carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, reflecting reliable garden performance in the UK climate. Like other agapanthus, it is drought-tolerant once established and flowers best when the clump is left slightly congested rather than divided too often.

common_name: Jacaranda Agapanthus (Dark-Striped Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Jacaranda is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar notable for a darker stripe pattern running down each blue petal.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, where arching strap-like foliage forms a dense clump. Jacaranda bears blue flowers marked with a darker central stripe down each petal, giving the flower heads a distinct veined or pin-striped look compared to solid-colored blue cultivars. It holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for garden-worthiness and reliable flowering. Established clumps tolerate dry spells well and are best left undisturbed for several years before dividing.

common_name: Hoyland Blue Agapanthus (White-and-Pale-Blue Bicolor Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Hoyland Blue carries the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its white flowers edged and flushed with pale blue.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, where clumps of narrow evergreen foliage support rounded flower heads on sturdy scapes. Hoyland Blue is a bicolor cultivar with predominantly white flowers softly marked and margined with pale blue, giving a frostier look than solid blue or solid white forms. The cultivar holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Once established it tolerates dry conditions well and benefits from mulch over winter in the coldest parts of its hardiness range.

common_name: Royal Blue Agapanthus (Bright Blue RHS Award-Winning Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Royal Blue is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar valued for its clear, bright blue flower color.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained soil; Royal Blue forms a clump of arching strap foliage topped in summer by dense, rounded heads of bright, saturated blue flowers on upright stems. It carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for consistent garden performance. Deadhead spent flower stems at the base to tidy the clump, and leave the evergreen foliage in place through winter in mild climates for continued interest. Drought-tolerant once established, it flowers most freely when slightly pot-bound.

common_name: Midnight Star Agapanthus (Deep Blue RHS Award-Winning Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Midnight Star is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar noted for unusually deep blue flower color.

directions: Site in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil. Midnight Star produces rounded umbels of deep, dark blue flowers that read noticeably darker than typical agapanthus blues, held above clumps of narrow arching foliage in summer. It holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. The clump is drought-tolerant once rooted in and performs best when left undivided for several years, since flowering declines temporarily after disturbance.

common_name: Purple Delight Agapanthus (Purple-Flowered RHS Award-Winning Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Purple Delight is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar grown for true purple, rather than blue-violet, flower color.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, where clumps of strappy evergreen foliage anchor rounded flower heads on tall scapes. Purple Delight stands out among agapanthus cultivars for genuinely purple rather than blue or violet-blue flowers, a color prized for mixed borders needing a true-purple accent in summer. It carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Water regularly the first season to establish, then reduce to occasional deep watering, as mature clumps are quite drought-tolerant.

common_name: Jonny's White Agapanthus (Pure White RHS Award-Winning Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Jonny's White holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its clean white flower heads.

directions: Grow in well-drained soil in full sun to encourage strong flowering; Jonny's White forms a clump of narrow arching foliage topped in summer by rounded umbels of pure white flowers. It carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, reflecting dependable performance in UK trial gardens. White-flowered agapanthus cultivars like this one are useful for brightening evening gardens and pairing with blue-flowered companions. Once established the clump needs little supplemental water beyond normal rainfall.

common_name: Megan's Mauve Agapanthus (Lavender-Blue RHS Award-Winning Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Megan's Mauve is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar with soft lavender-blue flower color.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Megan's Mauve bears rounded flower heads in a soft lavender-blue shade that leans toward mauve rather than true blue, held above clumps of strap-shaped evergreen leaves. The cultivar holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. It combines well with pink and silver-foliaged border companions thanks to its muted flower tone. Established clumps are drought-tolerant and flower most reliably when left undivided for several seasons.

common_name: Cahors Alstroemeria (Pink-and-Yellow RHS Award-Winning Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Cahors is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar reaching about 90 cm (35 in) tall with pink and yellow flowers.

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun, handling the brittle roots carefully to avoid breakage. Cahors bears pink flowers with a yellow throat on stems reaching roughly 90 cm, and carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for reliable garden performance. Pull rather than cut spent flowering stems from the base to stimulate continued rebloom through summer. In colder zones mulch heavily for winter protection, or lift and store the roots where winters are too severe for the hardiness range.

common_name: Coronet Alstroemeria (Tall Salmon-and-Yellow RHS Award-Winning Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Coronet is a tall RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar reaching about 140 cm (55 in) with salmon and yellow flowers.

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun, giving plants extra room since Coronet is one of the taller Peruvian lily cultivars at around 140 cm. It bears salmon flowers with a yellow throat and holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Because of its height, a bit of shelter from strong wind keeps the flowering stems upright without staking. Pulling spent stems from the base rather than cutting them encourages continued bloom through the season.

common_name: Orange Glory Alstroemeria (Tall RHS Award-Winning Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Orange Glory is a tall RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar reaching about 150 cm (59 in).

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Orange Glory is among the tallest garden Alstroemeria cultivars, reaching roughly 150 cm, so site it toward the back of a border or against a fence for wind shelter. It carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for sustained garden performance. Pull rather than cut spent flowering stems at the base to encourage continued flowering through the season. Mulch heavily for winter protection in the colder part of its hardiness range.

common_name: Oriana Alstroemeria (Compact Salmon-and-Yellow RHS Award-Winning Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Oriana is a compact RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar reaching only about 50 cm (20 in).

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Oriana stays notably compact at around 50 cm, making it well-suited to the front of a border or a large container, unlike many taller Peruvian lily cultivars. It bears salmon flowers with a yellow throat and carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Pull spent flowering stems from the base rather than cutting them to stimulate continued bloom. Protect with mulch over winter where temperatures approach the lower end of its hardiness range.

common_name: Phoenix Alstroemeria (Red-and-Yellow RHS Award-Winning Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Phoenix is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar reaching about 100 cm (39 in) with red and yellow flowers.

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun, handling the brittle roots carefully. Phoenix bears red flowers with a yellow throat on stems to about a meter tall, and holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Pull rather than cut spent flowering stems from the base to encourage continued bloom through the growing season. Mulch heavily for winter protection in colder parts of its hardiness range, or lift and store roots where winters are too severe.

common_name: Sonata Alstroemeria (Red-and-Yellow RHS Award-Winning Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Sonata is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar reaching about 100 cm (39 in) with red and yellow flowers.

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun. Sonata produces red flowers with a yellow throat on meter-tall stems and carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for dependable garden performance. Pulling rather than cutting spent flowering stems from the base removes the seed-forming stem entirely and encourages continued rebloom. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring if flowering declines.

common_name: Yellow Friendship Alstroemeria (Tall Hardy RHS Award-Winning Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Yellow Friendship is a tall, hardy RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar reaching about 140 cm (55 in), related to the classic cultivar 'Friendship'.

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Yellow Friendship grows considerably taller than the related cultivar 'Friendship', reaching around 140 cm, and is rated among the hardier garden Alstroemeria selections. It holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Pull rather than cut spent flowering stems from the base to encourage rebloom through the season. Its relatively greater cold tolerance makes it a reasonable choice for the cooler end of the Alstroemeria hardiness range, though winter mulch is still worthwhile.
